Consider an AR(2) model defined by: Yt = ϕ1Yt−1 + ϕ2Yt−2 + εt where εt i.i.d.∼N(0,σ2) are independent white noise errors.

We will compare four parameter estimation methods through a Monte Carlo simulation.

Consider the full likelihood for that model. Following the approach from the slides, the full likelihood includes the unconditional density of (Y1,Y2) under stationarity: L(η) where η= [ϕ1,ϕ2,σ2]⊤, (Y1,Y2) follows a multivariate normal distribution with a covariance matrix of dimension 2 ×2 with its entries corresponding to γ(0) and γ(1) derived in Exercise 1, and f is the density function of the Gaussian distribution. 


```{r}
#rm(list = ls())

autocovariance_0 <- function(sigma, phi1, phi2) { 
  var <- sigma^2
  
  gam0 <- (var*(1-phi2))/(1-phi2-((phi1^2)*(1+phi2))-(phi2^2)+(phi2^3))
  
  gam0

}

autocovariance_1 <- function(sigma, phi1, phi2) {

  gam0 <- autocovariance_0(sigma, phi1, phi2)

  gam1 <- (phi1 / (1 - phi2)) * gam0

  gam1
}

# 2. Implement a function that computes the full log-likelihood using the results from Exercise 1 and from the previous point:

log_likelihood <- function(sigma, phi1, phi2, Y, T) {

  gam0 <- autocovariance_0(sigma, phi1, phi2)
  gam1 <- autocovariance_1(sigma, phi1, phi2)

  var <- sigma^2

  # Initial log-likelihood: density of (Y1, Y2)
  L_initial <- -log(2*pi) -
    0.5*log(gam0^2 - gam1^2) -
    ((gam0*(Y[1]^2 + Y[2]^2) -
        2*gam1*Y[1]*Y[2]) /
       (2*(gam0^2 - gam1^2)))

  # Calculate residuals for t = 3, ..., T
  residual <- numeric(T)

  for (t in 3:T) {
    residual[t] <- Y[t] - phi1*Y[t-1] - phi2*Y[t-2]
  }

  # Conditional log-likelihood
  L_conditional <- -((T-2)/2)*log(2*pi*var) -
    (1/(2*var))*sum(residual[3:T]^2)

  # Full log-likelihood
  L <- L_initial + L_conditional

  return(L)
}

```

```{r}
# Test the function:

set.seed(123)

Y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
  model = list(ar = c(0.9, -0.7)),
  n = 30,
  sd = 5
))

log_likelihood(
  sigma = 5,
  phi1 = 0.9,
  phi2 = -0.7,
  Y = Y,
  T = length(Y)
)


```
Implement a function that computes the conditional log-likelihood.

```{r}

# Conditional likelihood:

conditional_log_likelihood <- function(sigma, phi1, phi2, Y, T) {

  var <- sigma^2

  # Calculate residuals for t = 3, ..., T
  residual <- numeric(T)

  for (t in 3:T) {
    residual[t] <- Y[t] - phi1*Y[t-1] - phi2*Y[t-2]
  }

  # Conditional log-likelihood
  L_conditional <- -((T-2)/2)*log(2*pi*var) -
    (1/(2*var))*sum(residual[3:T]^2)

  return(L_conditional)
}

# Test:

set.seed(123)

conditional_log_likelihood(
  sigma = 5,
  phi1 = 0.9,
  phi2 = -0.7,
  Y = Y,
  T = length(Y)
)

```

Implement the OLS estimator for the AR(2) model. Set up the least squares problem as: Y= Fϕ+ ε:

```{r}

# OLS estimation for an AR(2) model

ols_estimation <- function(Y, T) {

  # Response variable: Y3, ..., YT
  Y_response <- Y[3:T]

  # Matrix of predictors: Y(t-1) and Y(t-2)
  F <- cbind(
    Y[2:(T-1)],
    Y[1:(T-2)]
  )

  # OLS estimator: (F'F)^(-1) F'Y
  phi_hat <- solve(t(F) %*% F) %*% t(F) %*% Y_response

  phi1_hat <- phi_hat[1]
  phi2_hat <- phi_hat[2]

  # Calculate residuals
  residual <- Y_response - F %*% phi_hat

  # Estimate the innovation variance
  sigma2_hat <- sum(residual^2) / (T-2)

  return(list(
    phi1_hat = as.numeric(phi1_hat),
    phi2_hat = as.numeric(phi2_hat),
    sigma2_hat = as.numeric(sigma2_hat)
  ))
}

ols_estimation(Y, length(Y))

```

6. Generate B = 500 time series from the AR(2) model with parameters ϕ1 = 0.9, ϕ2 =−0.7, σ= 5, and sample size n= 30. For each generated series, obtain ϕ1_hat, ϕ2_hat, σ2_hat using:

• Conditional likelihood maximization (using optim)
• Full likelihood maximization (using optim)
• Least squares estimation
• Built-in fable::ARIMA function

```{r}
library(fable)
library(tsibble)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

B <- 500
n <- 30

phi1 <- 0.9
phi2 <- -0.7
sigma <- 5

# Create a place to store the results

results <- matrix(NA, nrow=B, ncol=12)

colnames(results) <- c(
  "phi1_cond", "phi2_cond", "sigma2_cond",
  "phi1_full", "phi2_full", "sigma2_full",
  "phi1_ols", "phi2_ols", "sigma2_ols",
  "phi1_arima", "phi2_arima", "sigma2_arima"
)

# Generate a series and estimate its parameters

for (b in 1:B) {

  Y <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    model = list(ar = c(phi1, phi2)),
    n = n,
    sd = sigma
  ))

  start <- c(0.5, -0.3, log(5))

  # Estimate using conditional likelihood
  fit_cond <- optim(par = start, fn = function(par) {
    -conditional_log_likelihood(
      sigma = exp(par[3]),
      phi1 = par[1],
      phi2 = par[2],
      Y = Y,
      T = length(Y)
    )
  })

  results[b, 1:3] <- c(
    fit_cond$par[1],
    fit_cond$par[2],
    exp(fit_cond$par[3])^2
  )
  
  # Estimate using full likelihood
  fit_full <- optim(par = start, fn = function(par) {
    -log_likelihood(
      sigma = exp(par[3]),
      phi1 = par[1],
      phi2 = par[2],
      Y = Y,
      T = length(Y)
    )
  })

  results[b, 4:6] <- c(
    fit_full$par[1],
    fit_full$par[2],
    exp(fit_full$par[3])^2
  )
  
  # Estimate using OLS
  fit_ols <- ols_estimation(Y, length(Y))

  results[b, 7:9] <- c(
    fit_ols$phi1_hat,
    fit_ols$phi2_hat,
    fit_ols$sigma2_hat
  )
  
  
  # Add the fourth method: fable::ARIMA
  data <- tsibble(
    time = 1:n,
    y = Y,
    index = time
  )

  fit_arima <- data %>%
    model(ARIMA(y ~ 0 + pdq(2, 0, 0)))
  

  arima_est <- tidy(fit_arima)
 

  results[b, 10] <- arima_est$estimate[arima_est$term == "ar1"]
  results[b, 11] <- arima_est$estimate[arima_est$term == "ar2"]
  results[b, 12] <- glance(fit_arima)$sigma2

}


```

Checking the results

```{r}
# True values:
# phi1 = 0.9
# phi2 = -0.7
# sigma2 = 25

head(results)

# Average estimate from each method:

colMeans(results, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Create boxplots showing the distribution of the four estimators for each parameter (ϕ1, ϕ2, σ2),
with horizontal lines indicating the true parameter values.

```{r}

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

# Estimates of phi1
boxplot(results[, c(1, 4, 7, 10)],
        names = c("Conditional", "Full", "OLS", "ARIMA"),
        main = expression(hat(phi)[1]),
        ylab = "Estimate")
abline(h = 0.9, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Estimates of phi2
boxplot(results[, c(2, 5, 8, 11)],
        names = c("Conditional", "Full", "OLS", "ARIMA"),
        main = expression(hat(phi)[2]),
        ylab = "Estimate")
abline(h = -0.7, col = "red", lty = 2)

# Estimates of sigma squared
boxplot(results[, c(3, 6, 9, 12)],
        names = c("Conditional", "Full", "OLS", "ARIMA"),
        main = expression(hat(sigma)^2),
        ylab = "Estimate")
abline(h = 25, col = "red", lty = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
